main_text.l: verb. 18. Qui invenit mulierem bonam, in-
venit bonum, & hauriet iucunditatem à Do-
mino: & ut hîc legimus, Numerus dierum
illius duplex est. Eorum enim vita pro iu-
cunditate & fide diutius perseverat. Ani-
mus enim, gaudens floridam facit ætatem.
Zelus autem & iracundia minuent dies, &
ante tempus senectam cogitatus molestus
adducet, Eccles. 30. Melior quoque mors
quàm vita amara: quin & melius est modico
tempore vivere cum iucunditate, quàm diu-
tius cum cordis amaritudine. Ideo pergit
Sapiens & dicit, (praecedentem versum cla-
rius exponens) Mulier fortis oblectat vi-
rum suum, & annos vitæ illius in pace imple-
bit. Fortis mulier intelligitur fidelis, solida,
virtuosa & constans in bono, [?]ἀνδρεία, etiam si
corpore fragilior fit & mollior, quæ scilicet
strenuè instat familiæ & domui gubernan-
dæ, ist heuslich / mannlich / fœmineum inge-
nium masculo animo excitans, 2. Mach. 7.
omnia agens virili animo, [?]חיל Prou. 31.
& 12. minimè otiosa, dissoluta aut vana. Hu-
iusmodi oblectat virum suum, in conversatio-
ne iucunda, pacifica, honesta, cū qua diutius
vivit, quia tranquillè usq; ad finem vitæ: non
enim senem exhorrescet, sed in primo amore
perseverabit semper: non enim tantùm car-
nalis est amor ut tabescat cum tempore, sed
virtuosus, qui cū virtute & canicie semper
maturescit. Posse aut & mulierem fortem &
dici & esse testatur etiā Socrates, qui dicebat

page.notes: Page number read as 235; the scan is slightly blurred at the numerals. Greek word (ἀνδρεία) and Hebrew word (חיל) are read from a small, blurred print and are marked [?]. The black letter words "heuslich" and "mannlich" are read as "häuslich" and "männlich" in the German print; the first is partly blurred. The first line begins with a fragment, "verb. 18.", from "Prouerb.", and the paragraph continues from the previous page. The strip of short marks under the last line looks like show-through or a rule and is not transcribed.
